significance: A thirteenth-century Vishnu temple at Madhab village near Niali, built by the Eastern Ganga king Ananga Bhima Deva III and holding a rare Madhava image. Its plan parallels the Sakhigopal and Ananta Vasudeva temples, and it preserves an old black sandstone Garuda and carvings drawn from the Krishna Lila and the Mahabharata.
